option_title: Conductivity-conditioned generation of disordered Li-halide solid electrolytes
question: Does conductivity-conditioned generation of disordered Li-halide electrolytes raise the hit rate for fast Li conductors over unconditioned generation as more candidates are screened?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning MatterGen's adapter on MLIP-predicted conductivity shifts generated halides toward fast Li conductors, because property conditioning already worked for bulk modulus [s_mattergen_5000].

compute_axis.quantity: generated candidate crystal structures screened per arm

held_fixed: Chemistry restricted to Li3MX6 halides (M = group-3/13/15 + lanthanides, X = halogen)
MatterGen base weights and the <=20-atom unit-cell generation limit
Hit threshold of 1 mS/cm predicted room-temperature conductivity
Single conductivity surrogate (GNN regressor calibrated on fine-tuned MACE MLIP-MD)

predictions.if_lever: At 100,000 screened candidates the conditioned arm's hit rate exceeds unconditioned generation's, and the gap widens with candidate count [s_mattergen_saturate].
predictions.if_not: The hit-rate gap between conditioned and unconditioned generation stays within seed-to-seed noise at every level, including 100,000 candidates.
predictions.decision_rule: Conditioned hit rate must exceed the unconditioned hit rate by >= 2x at the 100,000 level, with non-overlapping bootstrap 95% confidence intervals across 3 seeds.
predictions.noise_rule: 3 seeds per arm and level; bootstrap 95% confidence intervals on hit rate; the gap is real only when conditioned and unconditioned intervals do not overlap.
predictions.expected_why: MatterGen's adapter conditioning moved bulk-modulus generation to an extreme tail with only 5,000 labels, so conductivity conditioning should shift halide hits.

compute_tested_why: The test varies candidate structures screened per arm (1,000/10,000/100,000); more parallel GPUs buy more screened candidates per hour, moving directly along the compute axis.
scored_against: Conditioned hit rate is compared with the unconditioned arm's hit rate (same seeds and surrogate) and with the known-ICSD hit rate, at the 1 mS/cm threshold.

arms.what: MatterGen adapter fine-tuned on predicted log-conductivity, sampling the Li3MX6 halide space targeting high conductivity.
Base MatterGen sampling the same Li3MX6 halide chemical space with no property condition.
Known Li-halide solid electrolytes from ICSD screened by the same conductivity surrogate (fixed set).

baseline.what: Unconditioned generation arm (A2) and known ICSD Li-halide conductors (A3), screened by the identical surrogate.
baseline.value: Hit rate at the 1 mS/cm threshold; known Li3MX6 conductors report ~1-10 mS/cm

anchor.what: Reproduce MatterGen's 38.57% S.U.N. rate on 1,024 unconditional samples before trusting generation.

checks: MACE-MP-0b2-large halide fine-tune reproduces ~10.0 meV/atom energy RMSE on a held-out DTU subset.
Conductivity surrogate's predicted-vs-MLIP-MD conductivity Pearson r >= 0.6 on held-out calibration structures.
Generated Li3MX6 candidates parse as valid pymatgen structures and dedupe via StructureMatcher.
Top-candidate MLIP-NEB migration barriers rank consistently with the surrogate's conductivity ordering.

phases.what: Download MatterGen + MACE-MP-0b2 checkpoints and a DTU-DB subset; reproduce both anchors; measure real gen_rate and MACE step time.

gate.else: Stop; environment or checkpoints are broken, fix before any further spend.

phases.what: Fine-tune MACE-MP-0b2-large; run MLIP-MD on 80 calibration structures; train and validate the surrogate; label 10,000 structures.
phases.stop_rule: finetune_mlip_hours A100-hours + label_md_hours A6000-hours + surrogate_hours A6000-hours.

gate.else: Double the calibration MD (line L2b) and cut the 100,000 level to 50,000 to stay under budget_usd.

phases.what: Fine-tune the MatterGen adapter on the 10,000 surrogate conductivity labels.
phases.stop_rule: adapter_hours A100-hours or validation loss plateaus.

phases.what: Generate A1 and A2 candidates at 1,000/10,000/100,000; pull the ICSD Li-halide set for A3.
Supercell + site-disorder sampling, surrogate screening, dedupe, per-arm per-level hit rates.
MLIP-NEB (fine-tuned MACE) on the top-10 candidates per arm.
Bootstrap confidence intervals across seeds; apply the decision rule.

restructuring.sequential_part: Conductivity labels feed adapter fine-tuning, then conditioned generation, screening, and NEB validation—five dependent steps.
restructuring.method: None—labels, generation, and screening are independent per structure and run side by side across GPUs.

scope_gap: DFT-level (VASP/AIMD) conductivity and DFT-NEB validation—Lambda GPU nodes carry no VASP license; NEB validation is MLIP-NEB anchored to the published 619-value DFT barrier dataset.
Experimental synthesis and impedance measurement of any candidate.

novelty.closest_prior: MatterGen's adapter fine-tuning shifted bulk-modulus generation toward extreme values with only 5,000 labels, but never conditioned on ionic conductivity or disordered halides.
novelty.left_open: No one has conditioned crystal generation on ionic conductivity for disordered halides, nor measured whether more candidates widens the conditioned hit-rate gap.

limits: Shows only MLIP-predicted conductivity, not DFT or measured; halide family only; no synthesis.
test_summary: Fine-tune MACE-MP-0b2 on DTU's 400k halide database, label with MD-predicted conductivity, fine-tune MatterGen's adapter, generate 1k/10k/100k candidates per arm, screen, NEB-validate top ten, compare hit rates.

sources.quote: It contains approximately 400k density functional theory (DFT) calculated structures with energies, forces, and stresses, together with hierarchical metadata, providing a resource to accelerate the discovery and optimization of halide electrolytes.

We demonstrate the utility of the database by fine-tuning the MACE-MP-0b2-large foundation model: the energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) decreased from 154.8 to 10.0 meV atom-1 and the all-force-component RMSE from 168.3 to 39.0 meV A-1 on a held-out test set, confirming that domain-specific training data is necessary for structurally disordered halide configurations.
